holes.note: Slate Gate: a long, narrow opener: bunkers pinch the drive at 270, pot bunkers guard the green
The Causeway: out of reach in two: a narrow causeway between the pit and the slate waste, the bar bunker across the lay-up
The Pit: downhill to an island green in the old pit; the land bridge is front right
Quarry Dog: dogleg left round a flooded pit: carry the corner or play out right for a long second
The Crown: driveable with a perfect strike, but the green sits in a crown of pot bunkers; the lay-up has a pond right
Slate Sea: all carry over a sea of slate waste; the bail-out apron is left, a pond waits right
The Serpent: an S down the valley; the creek crosses at 335 and again just short of the green
The Chute: out of a chute of pines to an elevated green: the longest par 4 on the course
Home Pit: water all down the left, the green on a peninsula; bail out right into the sand
Split Decision: a field of bunkers splits the fairway: left is shorter, right gives the better angle
Thimble: the smallest green on the course in a ring of pot bunkers, water long
The Leap: carry the pond off the tee, then lay up right of the water or take on the long carry to the green
Long Climb: long and uphill, bunkers staggered either side of the drive
The Hook: dogleg right round a stand of pines; water right of the green
The Abyss: over a flooded pit; the long way round on the left is dry
Twin Pits: two pits squeeze the driving zone; lay up short of them for a long second
Last Island: the green is an island: the brave go over the water, the land bridge comes in from the lay-up on the right
The Gauntlet: water down the whole left side and in front of the green, bunkers right: hold your nerve
